name: Escape routes, muster points, signs and safety lighting
description: Arrangements that let personnel reach muster and embarkation stations: at least two widely separated means of escape, marked routes, photoluminescent strip indicators, emergency lighting, assembly/mimic plans, EEBDs and handrail strength requirements. Sources are SOLAS II-2/13, IMO MODU Code, classification and regulator pages. Primary source: https://www.imorules.com/GUID-FD648BB1-3991-407E-AD5E-1263AA7F3AD4.html
aliases: Escape routes, muster points, signs and safety lighting

specifications.metric: Escape route marking and emergency light — Number of means of escape
specifications.unit: widely separated means from all spaces or group of spaces

specifications.metric: Escape route marking and emergency light — Strip indicator height above deck
specifications.basis: SOLAS II-2/13.3.2.5.1: escape routes marked by lighting or photoluminescent strip indicators placed not more than 300 mm above deck at all points including angles and intersections

specifications.metric: Escape route marking and emergency light — Maximum dead-end corridor length
specifications.basis: SOLAS II-2/13.3.3.4 for cargo ships; IMO 2009 MODU Code 9.4.1.3 and RS Class Rules 9.2.6 (search extracts)

specifications.metric: Escape route marking and emergency light — Quick-release escape door force
specifications.basis: SOLAS II-2/13.3.2.6.2: latch releases when force not exceeding 67 N applied; actuating bar at least 760 mm and not more than 1120 mm above deck

specifications.metric: Escape route marking and emergency light — Handrail / handhold strength
Escape route marking and emergency light — Minimum clear width of escape stairway with single escape
specifications.basis: SOLAS II-2/13.3.2.1.2 with handrails on both sides

specifications.metric: Escape route marking and emergency light — Minimum EEBDs in accommodation
specifications.basis: SOLAS II-2/13.3.4.2: all ships shall carry at least two emergency escape breathing devices within accommodation spaces
46 CFR 109.301(d)(3): 'The general alarm system must be tested' under weekly inspections and tests
